subject: HelmShift bakeoff results and retention proposal
messages:
From: Jordan Reeves <jordan@helmshift.io>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-09T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Bakeoff initial readout: performance concerns

Mina —

Thanks for running the side-by-side with CompetitorX last week. The engineering team ran our internal traffic profile against both stacks and we have two immediate concerns: p95 latency on 8k token requests is ~1.1s worse on Redwood (observed at peak), and sustained concurrency beyond 1200 rps starts to exacerbate tail latency. Those are our two gating items for a renewal + expansion.

We like the feature set and control plane, but the buyer committee is now asking for an explicit remediation plan and production-proofed numbers before we sign on to a renewed 6–12 month term that includes the planned upsell.

Can you share a concise proposal: dedicated capacity sizing recommendation, a focused benchmark plan we can run in our environment (or you run with our harness), and any commercial flex you can offer if we commit to a 6‑month term now? Also loop in procurement (copied).

Jordan
VP Product — HelmShift
From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Reeves <jordan@helmshift.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-09T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Bakeoff initial readout: performance concerns

Jordan — thanks for the clear note and the data callout. We take p95 and concurrency very seriously.

Action plan (high level):
- We can run a focused 48-hour side-by-side using your harness (or run our harness against a recorded trace you provide).
- Karthik (Solutions Architect) will produce a recommended dedicated pool configuration (GPU type, counts, batching and KV cache config) tuned to your 8k token workload.
- We will include a quantitative p50/p95/p99 latency profile and cost-per-token delta vs your competitor across realistic QPS buckets.
- Commercially: we can propose a short-term retention package for 6 months that includes a capacity guarantee and a term discount — I’ll loop Ben for pricing flex.

Karthik/Ben — can you pick this up Monday and propose the bench plan + a draft term sheet? Jordan — if you can share the harness link or a replay trace, that will speed things up.

Cheers,
Mina Haddad

Date: 2026-12-10T08:45:00-08:00
Subject: HelmShift focused benchmark plan + preliminary results

Team / Jordan —

Attached: helmshift_benchmark_results_20261210.pdf (summary) and raw trace config used for the run. High level findings from the 24-hour focused run we executed against the trace you shared: 

Summary numbers (median of several runs):
- Model variant: redwood-instruct-7b (quantized int8) vs redwood-instruct-7b (fp16) and CompetitorX-standard
- Sustained throughput target: 1200 rps (your target). Achieved: 1280 rps with p50=180ms, p95=430ms (fp16), p95=490ms (int8) under recommended batching.
- Peak stress (burst to 2000 rps): p95 observed at 820ms under our 4x A100 equivalent pool with async batching enabled (KV cache warm). CompetitorX in the same test had p95 ~1.3s.
- Latency variance driven by long context GC and cold KV cache hits; we reduced tail by enabling aggressive prefix caching and lowering max_batch_delay to 12ms.

Recommendation (production sizing):
- Dedicated pool: 4 x A100-equivalent instances (can be offered as a dedicated cluster or reserved burst capacity).
- Autoscale headroom: keep burst pool to 1.5x baseline for predictable peaks.
- Software tuning: enable prefix/KV persistent cache + async batching; retune max_batch_delay by environment.
- Expected monthly incremental cost (approx): $42k/month for the recommended pool (3–4% unit-cost increase vs CompetitorX depending on your request mix).

Commercial levers Mina/Ben to consider:
- 12-month commitment: 12% list discount + priority capacity reservation.
- 6-month commitment: 6% list discount + one-time migration/benchmark credit and a dedicated capacity SLA.

I’ve attached the full result PDF with plots and the precise config used. Happy to walk through the numbers with your infra team.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.ai

Karthik — thanks for the thorough run and the PDF. A few notes from our side after sharing with infra and procurement: 

- The numbers look reasonable and better than CompetitorX on peak stress, however procurement flagged price delta against our forecast. CompetitorX has pushed a limited 6‑month deal at 20% off + two migration days and direct infra support; we need Redwood to match aggressionally if we are to avoid swapping.
- Our legal/procurement are asking for: (1) a dedicated capacity SLA (uptime + latency SLO), (2) a mutual action plan with milestones and contacts, and (3) a one-page term summary for procurement/PO routing.

If Redwood can deliver a 6‑month retention package that includes a dedicated 3‑GPU guaranteed pool (with ability to burst), a one-time benchmarking/migration credit, and an explicit escalation SLA, we can move procurement to place a PO quickly. Can you get me a DocuSign link + mutual action plan by end of tomorrow?

Jordan

- SLA: 99.9% service availability for inference endpoints, and a latency escalation SLA (if observed p95 exceeds benchmarked p95 by >25% for two consecutive business days we trigger an ops war room with guaranteed response times).

2) Commercials
- Term: 6 months starting on PO acceptance.
- Discount: 8% off list for the committed portion of capacity; applied to the pricing_term_sheet_helmshift_20261211.pdf attached.
- One-time migration/benchmark credit: $10k (applied to first invoice).

3) Operational commitments
- We will provide a mutual action plan (attached spreadsheet) with named contacts, milestones (bench verification, cutover dry run, production switch), and escalation paths.
- One-day on-site (or two remote days) migration assistance included.

Next steps:
